clockgrove.authority_decisions: durable by decision: one immutable row per authorized command, never retired. It is the audit link from a privileged action to its principal and grants (PRD 22.2) and a foreign-key partner of its receipt, so it lives as long as the receipt
clockgrove.clock_admissions: bounded: at most one row per partition for native owners, whose every new admission deletes all other receipts; callers without an owner generation (tests) keep only current-generation, current-policy receipts ahead of committed simulation time (postgres-clock-admissions.ts admit)
clockgrove.command_receipts: durable by decision: one row per command, never retired. It is the idempotency record, and the code dedupes a command ID forever with no replay window (storedOutcome matches command_id and exact bytes; trusted continuation-chunk command IDs rely on it); world-reaction consumption verifies the source command's committed receipt (0024); its result carries the state hash the causal inspector verifies replay against; it anchors the authority decision. Grows with commands; any compaction (e.g. command_bytes behind the snapshot horizon, keeping request_hash) needs a bytes-free retry check first
clockgrove.inspector_accesses: bounded: 90-day window per tenant, retired on insert: each access deletes up to 100 of its tenant's rows older than 90 days (record_inspector_access, 0023); a tenant with no further access keeps its last rows until its next access; at most 300 rows per principal per tenant in any trailing hour (0028)
clockgrove.runtime_operator_actions: bounded: 90-day window per tenant, retired on insert: each operator action deletes up to 100 of its tenant's rows older than 90 days (record_runtime_operator_action, 0031); a tenant with no further action keeps its last rows until its next one; at most 300 rows per principal per tenant in any trailing hour (0031)
clockgrove.partition_schedules: bounded: pending rows are the live queue (removed only by completion); a done row is kept 90 days after completion (updated_at), then retired: each command that completes an occurrence deletes up to 100 of that partition's expired done rows (retire_done_schedules trigger, 0027); a partition with no further completions keeps its done rows until its next one
clockgrove.partition_states: bounded: one row per partition, updated in place; it is also the clock owner claim (generation, owner id) and one replaceable catch-up operation link; completion clears the link, a changed canonical policy clears it atomically, and retries update its fixed-size cursor and fairness stamp in place; the snapshot sweep's attempt stamp (snapshot_attempted_at, 0030) is one more fixed-size column updated in place
clockgrove_birth.birth_cognitive_seed_re: grows with world births: written once per birth, never retired
clockgrove_birth.birth_random_streams: grows with world births: written once per birth, never retired
clockgrove_birth.birth_schedules: grows with world births: written once per birth, never retired
clockgrove_birth.birth_space_state: grows with world births: written once per birth, never retired
clockgrove_birth.birth_state_sections: grows with world births: written once per birth, never retired
clockgrove_birth.pack_artifact_resources: grows with published pack versions per tenant, never retired
clockgrove_birth.pack_artifacts: grows with published pack versions per tenant, never retired
clockgrove_birth.pack_installations: grows with world births: one per installed pack, never retired
clockgrove_birth.world_birth_states: grows with world births: one per world, never retired
clockgrove.event_dispatches: unbounded: one row per dispatched event and channel; publication status and the once-written consumption disposition (consumed_at, consumed_principal_id) update that row in place, so duplicates add no rows; no retirement yet (follow-up: retire settled dispatches)
clockgrove_birth.provisioning_cases: grows with authorized births: one permanent row per case, never retired; it keeps the run identity and a small request header (authorization, case, artifact digests); the pack source (bytea, bounded by the SDK inventory limit) is held only while the case is open and released when it turns ready or failed; retries and reconciliation add no rows
clockgrove.conversation_sessions: bounded: at most 100 sessions that are not deleted per participant and world timeline (guard_conversation_session, 0034), updated in place (state, title, message count); delete is a terminal tombstone that hides the session from every API, and the row with its title artifact stays until Wave 9 RW-0902 crypto-shreds the conversation data key
clockgrove.conversation_messages: bounded per session: at most 1,000 immutable messages (0034), each naming one encrypted conversation artifact; grows with sessions, so by the session bound per participant; a deleted session's messages are unreadable through every API and stay, as ciphertext, until Wave 9 RW-0902 crypto-shreds the conversation data key
clockgrove.conversation_turns: bounded per session: at most 500 immutable turns, one per Caretaker message (0034); retired with their session's messages as conversation_messages says
clockgrove.conversation_participants: bounded: one immutable row per human participant of a session (exactly one for a Caretaker Talk session; 0034 offers no join), so it grows with conversation_sessions; retired with its session's messages as conversation_messages says
clockgrove.agent_runs: bounded per session: at most 2,000 runs (four attempts for each of a session's 500 turns; guard_agent_run, 0036), so by the session bound per participant; each run is updated in place once, from running to its one terminal disposition, and never again; it names one initial encrypted prompt artifact plus bounded research model-step prompt artifacts (0060), stored only after the run limit is checked, so a refused Talk adds none; a prompt that includes actor documents is a private_cognition artifact (0037) retired with the private_cognition data key, any other a conversation artifact retired with the conversation data key (a prompt whose run then fails to open is an orphaned artifact of its class, one per such failure); retired with its session's messages as conversation_messages says
clockgrove.run_steps: bounded per run: at most 32 steps (0036), each updated in place once, from running to its terminal disposition; grows with agent_runs and is retired with them; optional tool evidence is bounded metadata linking the retained call, grant, effect and encrypted result, never plaintext content
clockgrove.actor_documents: bounded: at most 256 documents per actor and world timeline (guard_actor_document, 0037); each row is a head pointer updated in place only by its version guard (current version, state); archive is a terminal state, and an archived document keeps its row and versions for the world's life by decision (issue 17)
clockgrove.actor_document_versions: bounded: at most 1,000 immutable versions per document (0037 CHECK) of at most 8,192 bytes each, so at most 256,000 per actor; kept for the world's life by decision (issue 17): manifests cite exact versions and reassembly reads them; a session summary's versions stay with their session's conversation data until Wave 9 RW-0902 crypto-shredding
clockgrove.document_change_sets: bounded: committed change sets each write 1 to 8 versions, so they are bounded by actor_document_versions; model proposals are at most one per run (UNIQUE run_id), so bounded by agent_runs; refused change sets are kept 90 days, then retired on insert: each refused change set deletes up to 100 of its tenant's refused rows older than 90 days (retire_refused_change_sets, 0037); operator change sets share the inspector rate limit of 300 per principal per hour (0028)
clockgrove.context_manifests: bounded: one immutable row per run (primary key run_id, 0037) of at most 273 metadata entries, so bounded by agent_runs; retired with its session's messages as conversation_messages says
clockgrove.conversation_turn_fibers: bounded per session: at most 1,000 turns, one per possible Caretaker message (guard_turn_fiber, 0038), each updated in place along its phases until its one terminal phase and never again; retired with their session's messages as conversation_messages says; research counters update in place and encrypted private-cognition history has at most the configured call limit (default three), with 8 KiB model excerpts per call; checkpoint artifacts and interrupted/orphaned model-step prompts remain encrypted under their class keys and retire with conversation/private-cognition data, bounded by session runs/steps and admitted research attempts
clockgrove.actor_processes: bounded: one row per actor process, updated in place (lease, checkpoint, segment count); grows with processes, which today only the fixture objective starts; no retirement yet, since a process keeps its identity for its actor's life
clockgrove.actor_process_segments: bounded per process: at most 64 immutable segments (0038), so it grows with actor_processes and is retired with them
clockgrove.actor_activation_policies: bounded: one row per actor and world timeline; at most 64 configurations with total JSON <=1 MiB, updated in place; lifetime model reservations and causal receipts limited to 1,000 (0039)
clockgrove.actor_activations: bounded: at most 1,000 causal receipts per actor, serialized by policy row counter (0039); no deletion, so a duplicate causal root remains suppressed for actor life
clockgrove.wake_triage: bounded per session: one immutable decision receipt per conversation turn fiber (at most 1,000 per session, 0038); reserved cost remains charged for unknown or interrupted calls. Retained with the session and its run evidence; no independent append stream beyond the existing turn limit (issue 111).
clockgrove_mcp.credentials: durable by decision (issue 164): one mutable encrypted envelope per random credential reference; no plaintext or canonical events. Revoked rows permanently retain their UUID, scope and irreversible fence, with ciphertext and wrapped key erased; never delete a tombstone or reuse its reference. Pending/blocked rows remain until explicit revoke by the owning installation lifecycle; installation lifecycle composition is a later part. Retain older key versions while live envelopes reference them.
clockgrove.mcp_installations: durable by decision (issue 164): one mutable installation row per operator installation, current bounded discovery and reviews updated in place. Revoked rows persist as irreversible tombstones for world lifetime; historical discoveries and reviews remain in the canonical Journal under its retention policy.
clockgrove.moderation_shadow: bounded per session: one private shadow annotation per inbound conversation turn fiber (at most 1,000 per session, 0038). Reserved before a model call and completed once; interrupted calls never repeat. Kept with conversation messages; deleted sessions hide annotations through participant authorization (issue 162).
clockgrove.channel_bindings: one immutable binding per private session, subject to the existing 100 non-deleted-session bound per participant/world/timeline; deleted session tombstones and bindings remain for world lifetime. Normalized inbound envelope artifacts use a deterministic ID per attempted input key, including an orphan when acceptance loses a busy-session race; retained as encrypted conversation data until Wave 9 crypto-shredding, like existing rejected-input artifacts (0049).
clockgrove.mcp_bindings: durable by decision (issue 164): one mutable policy row per scoped binding ID and installation; disabled rows remain as tombstones for world lifetime. Policy history and operator attribution remain in the canonical Journal. Each row is bounded to 128 KiB and updates in place; new binding IDs grow with explicit operator actions.
clockgrove.delivery_consent: one mutable opt-in and lifetime message-unit budget per recipient/actor/world/timeline; cumulative reservations never reset. Kept for world lifetime so consent changes cannot erase spent capacity (issue 168).
clockgrove.deliveries: durable by decision (issue 168): one immutable request and terminal decision per scoped dedupe key, or one delayed decision updated once to terminal; no deletion, preserving replay and deduplication for world lifetime. Solicited response requests are bounded to one canonical key per committed Talk pair within existing session message capacity and use a separate one-unit allowance without changing proactive consent. Content is an encrypted conversation artifact retained under conversation retention.
clockgrove.delivery_sink_receipts: durable by decision (issue 168): at most one immutable fake or preview sink receipt per accepted delivery, retained with its delivery for deduplication and replay; contains only a reference to encrypted content.
clockgrove.effect_intents: durable by decision (issue 165): one immutable scoped idempotency identity and bounded metadata record per call, with one terminal disposition; retained for world lifetime so historical replay never loses deduplication. Arguments stay in encrypted conversation artifacts under conversation retention. No runtime writer is exposed by the foundation.
clockgrove.effect_attempts: bounded per intent (issue 165): at most one attempt, updated once to success, failure or explicit uncertainty, retained with the intent for world lifetime. Unknown cost remains NULL and counted separately; no automatic resend. Results are encrypted conversation artifacts under conversation retention.
clockgrove.mcp_read_switches: Internal emergency configuration (issue 165): one mutable row per global/world/installation scope; retained for world lifetime; no runtime or actor access.
clockgrove.mcp_read_turn_budgets: Durable turn budget (issue 165): one row per canonical session/message fiber, including proactive activation fibers; cumulative worst-case reservations never refunded across run segments; retained with effect intents for world lifetime and replay.
clockgrove.mcp_read_admissions: Durable admission (issue 165): one immutable reference-only record per attempted effect, retained with effect intents for world lifetime. Admitted calls are bounded by turn capacity; refused proposals also retain their disposition, so rows grow with attempted calls. No actor or runtime writer is exposed by this foundation.
clockgrove.mcp_read_retry_refusals: Durable conflicting-retry evidence (issue 165): one immutable hash-only receipt per distinct conflicting proposal to a scoped admission, deduplicated by retry hash and retained with the original effect for world lifetime. Distinct refused proposals grow with attempted retries; no runtime or actor writer is exposed.
clockgrove.world_mcp_budgets: bounded (issue 167): one fixed-size counter row per existing Management principal, updated in place; database minute resets counts in the same row, never appends. Retained with that principal; deletion cascades this non-audit budget. No credential, scope, request content or connection state is stored.
clockgrove.effect_approvals: durable by decision (issue 166): one bounded metadata row per scoped approval identity, retained for world lifetime to preserve exact binding, human decision attribution and single consumption across replay. State updates in place; no plaintext arguments or credentials. Optional arguments reference encrypted conversation artifacts under conversation retention. Internal foundation exposes no runtime writer.
